transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2026-12-02
Start: 16:00 PST
Duration: 68 minutes (approx)
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE); Luis Ortega (Redwood SE); Nina Park (Redwood Solutions); Priya Nair (Lyra Head of ML); Samir Patel (Lyra Platform); Elena Rossi (Lyra Security); Tom Wilson (CTO); Jordan (intern)

Auto-generated Summary (may be imperfect):
Redwood demo: showing structured JSON outputs using schema-first approach, tool calling (orders, DB writes, external API), and guardrail fallbacks. Discussed Dedicated vs Hosted and data residency, SOC2/KMS. Agreed to pilot: Dedicated reserved pool + 2-week benchmark.

-- Transcript --
[00:00] Maya: Alright everyone, thanks for joining, we're gonna do a quick run through schema-first execution and how tool calling works end-to-end in the Console and API. I'll hand over to Luis for the technical bits in a minute.
[00:14] Priya: Thanks, Maya. Quick context — we have a production chat assistant that needs to call a few internal tools (inventory check, order create, and a billing lookup) and must emit strict JSON because downstream services process it automatically. Latency under 350ms p50 is ideal, but we can tolerate spikes up to 700 for edge cases.
[00:35] Luis: Great, so Redwood's JSON mode lets you declare a schema up front and the model is constrained to output that structure. We'll show the Console's schema editor and an API example. Also: we layer runtime guardrails so if the output doesn't validate, we can trigger a structured fallback or call a safe noop.
[00:52] Samir: Who usually writes the schema? Our ML team or infra? We have a lot of existing contract tests.
[01:05] Maya: Usually it's collaborative. ML drafts, infra integrates into the API contracts. Redwood's Console has importers for OpenAPI and can generate base JSON schemas to start from.
[01:21] Elena: Security question — where are those payloads stored and encrypted? We need KMS and HSM support and full audit logs.
[01:34] Nina: Yes, Redwood Private and Dedicated both integrate with customer KMS; we also provide audit logs with token-level tracing in the Console. We'll drop the SOC2 link after this call.
[01:48] Tom: Also curious about failure modes: if the model returns partial or malformed JSON, what happens?
[01:58] Luis: Two main strategies in the runtime: schema-enforced parsing and fallback policies. If an output doesn't validate, we can: 1) re-prompt with the same call (elastic retry), 2) run a repair step (another model pass) into a transformer that patches to valid JSON, or 3) route to a safe tool stub so downstreams don't see bad data. You can configure per-route policies in Console.
[02:21] Priya: Can you show an example?
[02:27] Luis: Sure, I'll switch to the Console. (noise, typing) Ok — here is the schema editor, I've got an order schema loaded. The top-level object is order_id, items: array of {sku, qty}, user: {id, email}, and optional meta: {source, confidence}.
[02:52] [Screen share glitch] Speaker 1: Sorry, flaky connection.
[03:02] Luis: No worries. Here's the API sample. We call POST /v1/generate with mode: json, schema: <base64...> or schema_id. Notice the tool hooks section — you can attach tool manifests that map to internal RPCs.
[03:22] Jordan (intern): Is the tool calling synchronous? We need to combine external API results in the response sometimes.
[03:31] Luis: You can do sync tool calls in the runtime but best practice is to keep model outputs deterministic — we recommend async: model returns a tool invocation record, runtime executes tool, then the app merges the result and does a final validation. For some flows we support direct function returns if you enable that in Dedicated.
[03:55] Priya: This is interesting. Our downstream expects stable JSON schemas for contract tests. How often do models drift and how do you detect regressions?
[04:11] Maya: Redwood Optimize can run automated evals against your prompt set and highlight quality regressions. It suggests quantization and model variant changes with cost estimates. We'll show an Optimize suggestion in a moment.
[04:25] Samir: For the Dedicated pool, what's the expected P50 and P95 for a llm-l8 style model? We plan for 300 token sequences avg.
[04:38] Luis: Depends on hardware and batch config. On A100 class Dedicated we often see ~180-220ms p50 for 300 tokens with continuous batching tuned, p95 around 520ms in production loads. If you need stricter SLOs we recommend smaller sequence windows or higher reserved capacity.
[04:58] Tom: The numbers sound reasonable. How do we benchmark? Can we do a head-to-head with our current provider?
[05:07] Maya: Absolutely — we can run a two-week benchmark using your prompt set. Redwood will provision a Dedicated test pool and run synthetic load to replicate your traffic patterns. We'll provide a results spreadsheet.
[05:20] Elena: And the data residency — does Dedicated keep data in our VPC?
[05:27] Nina: For Private deployments yes; Dedicated can be deployed in a customer VPC option too. We have options for on-prem packages for strictly regulated data.
[05:36] [10 minute jump]
[10:04] Luis: Back to tool calling: here's a failure scenario. Model returns a malformed array, missing commas; runtime detects JSON.parse error, marks as invalid, and per route we can set auto-repair = true which will do a repair pass limited to N tokens, or set fallback_tool = "noop_order_logger".
[10:28] Priya: Is that repair step deterministic? We're worried about subtle hallucinated fields creeping in.
[10:35] Luis: Repair is a constrained re-write using the same schema and an instruction template. It's not guaranteed but we log every repair and you can enable human review for repaired outputs. The fallback tool option keeps downstream safe.
[10:50] Priya: Ok that helps.
[11:02] Samir: Show me the code snippet for schema enforcement in the API.
[11:09] Luis: (reads) POST /v1/generate
{
  "model": "redwood-llm-x",
  "mode": "json",
  "schema_id": "ord-2026-lyra-v1",
  "prompt": "<user message>",
  "runtime": { "fallback": "repair", "repair_attempts": 1 }
}
[11:38] Maya: Note you can pin model variants and have a fallback variant (lower-cost quantized) if the primary is unavailable. That helps with cost/latency tradeoffs.
[11:51] Elena: About encryption: do we support customer-managed keys? We need HSM-backed key policies.
[11:58] Nina: Yes, Redwood Private and Dedicated support KMS integrations including HSM-backed keys. We'll include the KMS integration guide.
[12:08] [Screen share: Redwood Optimize view]
[12:15] Maya: Here's Optimize — it analyzed your typical payloads and suggests batching window 40ms and a quantization profile for this workload; estimated token cost reduction is ~28% with negligible quality delta.
[12:31] Priya: How does Optimize measure quality? Is it prompt-set based?
[12:37] Luis: It runs your evals — we call them 'golden prompts' — and computes metrics (schema validation rate, semantic accuracy) across model variants and quantization. It also surfaces cases where function/tool calling fails.
[12:52] Tom: If Optimize suggests quantization, can we opt to run the pilot with quantized models?
[12:58] Maya: Yes, for Dedicated we can provide quantized variants. For initial pilot we usually run both full-fp and quantized to compare.
[13:10] [Small cross talk — someone drops audio briefly]
[13:25] Priya: A couple of constraints: we must obey strict audit trails, SAML SSO only, and all PII must be redacted before retention. Can Redwood meet that?
[13:38] Nina: SAML SSO is supported. For PII we have configurable redaction hooks in the runtime and can apply token-level retention policies. We'll send the docs.
[13:52] Elena: Are audit logs exportable to our SIEM? We use Splunk.
[13:58] Maya: Yes, logs can stream to your SIEM with per-request metadata. We include JSON event schema in the docs.
[14:10] [20 minute mark — demo shifts to a live flow]
[20:05] Luis: I'm going to show a live run. User asks: "Place an order for SKU-4432, quantity 2, expedited". Model returns an array — the initial run intentionally produces a malformed JSON (we set up to demo repair).
[20:22] [demo noise — typing]
[20:31] Luis: Output: {order_id: "", items: [ {sku: "4432", qty: 2 } ] meta: {source: "chat"}} — missing quotes and trailing commas. Runtime flags it, repair kicks in (one attempt).
[20:48] Luis: Repair result: {"order_id":"ord_2783","items":[{"sku":"4432","qty":2}],"meta":{"source":"chat","confidence":0.98}} — validated.
[21:01] Priya: Nice. Where did ord_2783 come from? Was that generated or from a tool?
[21:09] Luis: In this demo it's synthetic; in your flow we'd typically have the model return a tool invocation for create_order and then your order service returns the canonical ID.
[21:20] Samir: Can we see the call trace?
[21:24] Luis: Console shows the trace: model output -> validation -> repair -> tool invocation (if configured) -> final merge. Each step has timing and token cost.
[21:39] Maya: Also note the Console exposes per-route policies — you can choose to block an invalid output from invoking external systems.
[21:49] Priya: That is key for us.
[22:00] [Noise: someone coughs]
[22:10] Maya: Quick question — what are your success metrics for the pilot?
[22:16] Priya: Primary: schema validation rate > 99%, p50 latency < 350ms, cost per 1k transactions below our current provider. Secondary: minimal manual repairs, full audit trail integration.
[22:29] Tom: Timeline: we'd like pilot in early Dec, run for two weeks, then decide on Dedicated commit by end of year.
[22:38] Maya: Sounds doable. We'll scope a 2-week pilot with Dedicated test pool.
[22:44] [30 minute marker — deep-dive on SDKs]
[30:01] Luis: Here's an SDK snippet for handling tool responses and performing final validation client-side. (reads) client.generate({model, mode: 'json', schema_id, runtime:{repair_attempts:1}}).then(res => { if (!validate(res.output)) { // log and escalate }})
[30:32] Jordan: Are there pre-built validators for our languages? We are mostly Go + Node.
[30:38] Luis: We provide validators for Node and Python; community-contributed Go bindings exist. We can share a Go validator example.
[30:46] Priya: About function calling — if the model calls an internal RPC, is the RPC spec versioned? We need contract evolution support.
[30:55] Maya: The tool manifest supports semantic versioning; Console can perform canary rollouts of new tool versions and rule-based routing so you can cut over gradually.
[31:08] Samir: Competitor question: we currently use ProviderX for endpoints. How is your pricing model compared?
[31:15] Maya: Hosted is per-token; Dedicated is reserved capacity + per-token; Optimize suggestions include cost delta estimates. We'll include side-by-side pricing in the follow-up.
[31:29] [40 minute marker — security deeper dive]
[40:02] Elena: Regarding SSO and RBAC: we need SCIM provisioning, role mappings, and audit hooks for admin changes.
[40:12] Nina: SCIM is supported; RBAC supports custom roles and per-route permissions. We also support API keys scoped to models or routes.
[40:24] Elena: Data retention: can we set zero retention for specific routes?
[40:30] Nina: Yes, retention policies are per-route — set to zero, a fixed window, or indefinite. We also support selectable redaction.
[40:42] Tom: For compliance we'll need a contract amendment. Does Redwood offer enterprise SLA addendum?
[40:49] Maya: Yes, enterprise legal and SLA terms are part of our Private/Dedicated contracts. We'll loop in sales legal.
[41:00] [50 minute marker — closing and recap]
[50:05] Maya: Recap: 1) We'll send pilot pricing and test pool plan, 2) Redwood to provide SOC2/KMS docs and SIEM event schema, 3) Luis will share schema examples, 4) Schedule pilot kickoff for 2026-12-09. Any other asks?
[50:25] Priya: Please include detailed benchmark plan and what success looks like in the pilot doc.
[50:30] Maya: Will do.
[50:33] Elena: We'll email our security questionnaire; please respond by Monday.
[50:37] Maya: Great.
[50:40] Tom: Thanks everyone.
[50:42] [Meeting ends at ~17:08 PST — recording stop]

References mentioned: Console schema editor, Redwood Optimize, Dedicated capacity, Private deployment, KMS/HSM, SOC2 docs, SIEM integration. Links to be provided in follow-up (pricing spreadsheet, security pack, schema examples).
